newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS-Factors to watch - April 11.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS-Factors to watch - April 11.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Friday morning:
** India's minority coalition government faces defeat in parliamentary vote of confidence
** Trust vote expected at 8 p.m. (1430 GMT) after day-long televised debate. Parliament convenes at 11 a.m. (0530 GMT)
** Prospects of snap poll looms large after the coalition's key ally and the largest opposition parties decide to vote against the government
** The markets seen focussed on parliamentary debate, unfolding political events
** Trading on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) ends 45 minutes before normal close at 2.45 p.m. (0915 GMT) to enable brokers complete weekly carry-forward charges
** The BSE to stay open on Saturday for trading due to political developments
** On Thursday, the Bombay benchmark index fell 52.51 points, or 1.44 percent, at 3,598.37
** The Delhi share index fell 16.02 points to 750.50, Calcutta 1.53 points to 100.12 and Madras 64.96 points to 3,451.02

** Indian pharmaceuticals firm Ranbaxy Laboratories Ltd on Thursday announced an 11 percent increase in its 1996/97 (April-March) net profit, a dramatic drop from a 20.6 percent jump in first-half earnings
The sharp slowdown was due to a decrease in income from
the firm's activities in money markets, which the company had ploughed into its core pharmaceuticals business, chairman Parvinder Singh said
"But our operating income has continued to rise, and our
operating margins are significantly higher than the 22 percent increase in sales," Singh told a news conference
** The Indian rupee INR= opens steady at 35.845/860 against the dollar
